definitions.explanation: A scene of terrible destruction, suffering, or ruin. Describes the aftermath of disasters, accidents, wars, or other catastrophic events.

examples.japanese: {惨状|さんじょう}を{目|め}にした。
{地震|じしん}の{惨状|さんじょう}がテレビで{報道|ほうどう}された。
examples.english: The devastating aftermath of the earthquake was reported on television.

examples.japanese: {救助隊|きゅうじょたい}が{現場|げんば}に{到着|とうちゃく}したとき、{想像|そうぞう}を{絶|ぜっ}する{惨状|さんじょう}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: When the rescue team arrived at the scene, unimaginable devastation lay before them.

notes:
USAGE:
{惨状|さんじょう} is a formal, serious word used in news reports, historical accounts, and literary descriptions. It conveys a scene so terrible that it shocks or overwhelms observers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {惨状|さんじょう}を{目|め}にする: to witness devastation
- {惨状|さんじょう}が{広|ひろ}がる: devastation spreads out
- {想像|そうぞう}を{絶|ぜっ}する{惨状|さんじょう}: unimaginable devastation
- {惨状|さんじょう}を{伝|つた}える: to convey the tragic scene

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {惨状|さんじょう}: tragic scene (emphasizes the visible aftermath)
- {惨事|さんじ}: disaster, tragedy (emphasizes the event itself)
- {被害|ひがい}: damage, harm (factual, quantifiable)
